To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a multi-component numerical leaching model (SBLEM), which was developed by coupling general chemical speciation and numerical leaching models, can be used to predict the leaching behavior from cement-treated MSW ash when the ash ANC and pH-solublity curves of metals are accurately described.
a multi-component numerical leaching model can predict the leaching behavior from a cement-treated ash from a municipal waste incinerator.
a multi-component numerical leaching model coupled with a chemical speciation code can reasonably simulate the dynamic leaching of metals from cement-treated MSW incinerator ash.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a multi-component numerical model to predict the leaching behavior from s/s wastes.
developing an efficient numerical model for predicting the leaching behavior from s/s wastes.
the development of a general numerical leaching model that can predict the leaching behavior from a wide range of s/s wastes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a numerical leaching model to evaluate the leaching behavior from s/s wastes can reduce experimental efforts and time and provide a better understanding of the mechanisms of leaching.
the results obtained with the SBLEM model are in reasonable agreement with the leaching data obtained with the TCLP.
SBLEM is a useful tool for the prediction of leaching behavior of cement-stabilized/solidified MSW incinerator ash and other s/s waste.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SBLEM is a useful tool to predict leaching behavior of s/s waste.
SBLEM is a useful tool for evaluating leaching behavior and predicting leachate composition of s/s wastes, and it may be used to evaluate and optimize the design of s/s waste forms.
the SBLEM model is an efficient tool for simulating the leaching behavior in cement-treated ash and may be used to predict long-term leaching behavior of s/s wastes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SBLEM approach is a promising tool for predicting contaminant leaching from s/s wastes.
the use of a speciation code to model the leaching behavior is a viable approach to predicting leaching behavior of s/s waste.
SBLEM simulations can provide a useful alternative to experimental leaching tests for assessing the leaching of contaminants from s/s wastes.
